paper.title: Encoding and control of orientation to airflow by a set of Drosophila fan-shaped body neurons
paper.published_claim: ventral P-FN airflow tuning is organized by cell-body hemisphere, with preferred directions clustered near approximately 45 degrees ipsilateral rather than by fan-shaped-body column

published_response_definition.per_trial_response: mean firing rate during response window minus mean firing rate during baseline window
published_response_definition.repeat_aggregation: mean across the five repetitions for each airflow direction
published_response_definition.preferred_direction_method: convert each of the eight mean directional spiking responses into a signed response vector at that airflow angle, then take the angle of their mean vector

program_a_normalized_target.hemisphere_fold: multiply angle by +1 for left cell-body hemisphere and -1 for right cell-body hemisphere so ipsilateral is positive
program_a_normalized_target.aggregate_statistic: circular mean of hemisphere-folded preferred-direction angles
program_a_normalized_target.uncertainty_rule: 95% percentile bootstrap confidence interval over recordings with 10000 resamples and deterministic seed 0

allowed_interpretation: published ventral P-FN physiology supports a type-level normalized airflow-direction prior organized by cell-body hemisphere
the hemisphere-folded preferred-direction geometry is a candidate navigation-independent Program A calibration target
forbidden_interpretation: absolute firing-rate amplitude transfers unchanged to MaleCNS PFNa/PFNm/PFNp body IDs
P-F2N3 recordings are exact body-ID homologs of MaleCNS PFNa/PFNm/PFNp
negative baseline-subtracted responses may be clipped before vector-angle calculation
navigation performance may choose recordings, archive members, normalization, uncertainty, or target statistic
the complete 117.49 GB release must be downloaded before the README/member map is audited
